title: No service-locator resolution inside handler or business logic bodies
statement: Services are declared as minimal API handler parameters or constructor parameters, letting the container inject them; code does not call `context.RequestServices.GetService<T>()` / `GetRequiredService<T>()` from inside a handler or business-logic method body. The one accepted exception is the composition-root shim needed to alias an existing singleton onto `IHostedService` (`AddHostedService(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<T>())`).
rationale: Handler-parameter injection is what makes a handler's real dependencies visible at the call site and in tests (see QS-DN-007/008 for how tests then construct these directly). Pulling a service out of `RequestServices` inside the body hides the dependency from the signature, breaks constructing the handler outside a request pipeline, and is easy to reach for as a shortcut around a lifetime mismatch instead of fixing the registration (QS-DN-003).

good.caption: Dependencies declared as parameters.

bad.caption: GuidelineStore pulled from RequestServices instead of declared as a parameter.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, contrasted against Program.cs's own single accepted exception (the hosted-service alias).
